verifiedFacts.claim: Thriller 40 quotes Bruce Swedien saying “Wanna Be Startin’ Somethin’” began with extensive percussion, including drum machines, live drums, and a Univox drum machine he believed was an SR55.

sourceRefs.label: Thriller 40 Bruce Swedien track-by-track article
sourceRefs.title: Bruce Swedien On ‘Thriller’ Track By Track - Thriller 40
sourceRefs.extract: It starts with a lot of percussion. There’s some drum machines and some live drums and other things. It’s a Univox drum machine. We actually used it a lot on the Brothers Johnson record, and we were using it at that time on Michael’s record as well. I think it’s an SR55.

limitations: One attributed recording/production statement retained; no musical analysis, lyric interpretation, or complete session reconstruction is claimed.

verifiedFacts.claim: Thriller 40 quotes Bruce Swedien saying “Baby Be Mine” used John Robinson on drums and that Michael Jackson recorded all his vocals on Swedien’s unpainted, unvarnished eight-foot-square drum platform.

sourceRefs.label: Thriller 40 Bruce Swedien track-by-track article
sourceRefs.title: Bruce Swedien On ‘Thriller’ Track By Track - Thriller 40
sourceRefs.extract: That’s John Robinson playing drums on my drum platform. I still use it and Michael did all his vocals on that drum platform. It’s unpainted, unvarnished, about eight feet square and by getting the sound source up off the floor, it prevented secondary pick-up if I was recording other instruments along with whatever was on the drum platform.

limitations: One attributed recording/production statement retained; no musical analysis, lyric interpretation, or complete session reconstruction is claimed.

verifiedFacts.claim: Thriller 40 quotes Bruce Swedien saying “The Girl Is Mine” was the first track recorded for Thriller and that Paul McCartney arrived prepared for the duet session.

sourceRefs.label: Thriller 40 Bruce Swedien track-by-track article
sourceRefs.title: Bruce Swedien On ‘Thriller’ Track By Track - Thriller 40
sourceRefs.extract: That was actually the first track we recorded for the album. It was a duet with Michael and Paul McCartney who was an absolute joy to work with. He was such a gentleman, he came to the studio prepared – Linda McCartney was with him and we had a fabulous time.

verifiedFacts.claim: Thriller 40 quotes Bruce Swedien saying Michael Jackson performed the wolf howls on “Thriller,” though some library material was also used.

verifiedFacts.claim: Thriller 40 quotes Bruce Swedien saying “Beat It” kept a stock Synclavier intro patch because Michael Jackson loved it, even though the production team wanted every sound to be unrecognizable and unique.

sourceRefs.label: Thriller 40 Bruce Swedien track-by-track article
sourceRefs.title: Bruce Swedien On ‘Thriller’ Track By Track - Thriller 40
sourceRefs.extract: Oh boy – the intro synth was a stock Synclavier patch; any Synclavier will make that sound. We liked it but we wanted everything to be unrecognisable, unique, so we didn’t want to use that sound, but Michael loved it and made us keep it.

verifiedFacts.claim: Thriller 40 quotes Bruce Swedien saying the “Billie Jean” bass was played by Louis Johnson of the Brothers Johnson and recorded through a DI with a UTC transformer for a warm low end.

sourceRefs.label: Thriller 40 Bruce Swedien track-by-track article
sourceRefs.title: Bruce Swedien On ‘Thriller’ Track By Track - Thriller 40
sourceRefs.extract: The bass on this was fantastic – the bass player is Louis Johnson from the Brothers Johnson and I picked him up with a DI, which I still have – it’s got a UTC transformer in it and I got it when I lived in Chicago and the low-end is incredible – very warm.

verifiedFacts.claim: Thriller 40 quotes Bruce Swedien saying “P.Y.T. (Pretty Young Thing)” used a lot of Minimoog, programmed by Michael Boddicker, who was the synth programmer present throughout the project.

sourceRefs.label: Thriller 40 Bruce Swedien track-by-track article
